info.title: Docmost Service Bridge (east-west)
info.summary: The east-west endpoints this Docmost fork EXPOSES to an integrating platform.
info.description:
These are the machine-to-machine endpoints the fork hosts for an integrating platform (the inverse direction of authorization-service.openapi.json, which the fork calls). They exist so an external identity/session broker can provision a fork-local shadow user and mint a Docmost session for it, re-check (and narrow) live realtime connections after a revocation, and (Phase C) administer workspace settings + spaces and read the content model WITHOUT the platform reaching into Docmost's database directly. They are NOT part of the public north-south API and are not browser-facing.

Mode: the whole surface is 404 unless the fork runs with AUTHZ_MODE=remote (RemoteOnlyGuard, checked BEFORE the secret). In AUTHZ_MODE=native there is no integrating platform and every route below returns 404 for all callers.

Auth: every request carries a shared service secret in the x-authz-service-secret header (PLATFORM_AUTHZ_SERVICE_SECRET). Each /api/service/* route additionally requires exactly one least-privilege scope: session:mint, users:provision, users:resolve, workspace:read, workspace:settings:write, spaces:read, spaces:write, pages:read, pages:authz:read, pages:import:read, content:read, content:search, attachments:read, changes:read. Today a single full-scope secret is issued; per-scope credentials can be added later with no contract change.

Security properties an integrator must understand:
  - Identity-mutating endpoints are keyed ONLY on the caller's opaque externalId. The fork derives the shadow email (externalId@shadow.wiki-v2.internal) and resolves its own default workspace, so a caller can never select an arbitrary Docmost identity, name a real/privileged/native account, or supply a workspace id. This is a strong narrowing, not impersonation.
  - The platform is the authorization authority: it performs the PDP decision (space/workspace administer, or the filter-then-retrieve authorized-id set) BEFORE calling these endpoints. The content read endpoints are a PRIVILEGED DATA PLANE, not a second gate: they return metadata for exactly the supplied ids and do NOT re-authorize. The security of the caller's /v1 surface rests entirely on it passing an authorized id set.
  - Fail-closed: not remote -> 404; unconfigured secret -> 503; missing/wrong secret -> 401; wrong scope -> 403; over the per-credential rate limit -> 429; invalid body -> 400.

Response shape (incident #181): every 2xx body is EXACTLY the schema declared for its operation. The fork's global { data, success, status } response envelope (upstream TransformHttpResponseInterceptor) is skipped on this whole surface via per-handler @SkipTransform(); an integrator that receives an envelope is talking to a mis-built fork. Bring-up precondition: until Docmost first-run setup (POST /api/auth/setup) has created a workspace row, EVERY operation answers HTTP 404 with message exactly "Workspace not found" (an upstream pre-handler that runs before the service-bridge guards). That status + message pair is the ONLY response a consumer may treat as "no workspace provisioned yet"; any other 404 (e.g. the bare "Not Found" the fork answers when not in AUTHZ_MODE=remote) is a configuration error, and any 2xx body that does not match its declared schema is a contract violation the consumer must fail closed on.

Access-narrowing propagation (1.6.0, #501): a successful response from a route that can take access away (archiveSpace, addSpaceMember — an upsert can demote —, changeSpaceMemberRole, removeSpaceMember; and the native narrowing routes the integrator relays) carries `Authz-Propagation: confirmed | pending`. `confirmed` = the fork asked the integrator's OPTIONAL `POST /sync/settle` (authorization-service.openapi.json) and it answered that every access change committed up to this response is enforced; `pending` = the change is committed but could not be shown enforced within the bound (an integrator without /sync/settle always gets `pending`). The header never changes the status or the body, and it is absent in AUTHZ_MODE=native or when AUTHZ_NARROWING_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS=0. A consumer must treat an ABSENT header as unknown, never as confirmed.

Page structure (1.7.0, wiki-v2 #493/#545): `POST /api/service/authz/pages/state` serves the CURRENT authorization structure of pages (placement, restriction, restriction lineage), so an integrator can project it level-triggered instead of trusting event payloads. And in AUTHZ_MODE=remote the fork installs database guards that refuse to take a restriction away by anything but an explicit unrestrict or a purge: a native move-to-space of a restricted page or of a page in a restricted section, and a re-parent or restore-detach that takes an unrestricted page out from under its last restricted ancestor. The native routes the integrator relays answer those refusals (and a move cycle) with `409 { message, code }`, `code` one of `ccc_page_no_cycle`, `ccc_page_restricted_space_move`, `ccc_page_restriction_strip`; the whole write is rolled back.

Conditional page operations (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): `pageLifecycleState` also reports the page's own `position`. And, beside the native page routes an integrator relays as the acting user (NOT part of this /api/service surface), the fork serves atomic compare-and-write twins — `POST /api/pages/conditional-delete`, `conditional-move`, `conditional-move-to-space`, `conditional-update-meta` — each taking the native body plus `expectedEtags` (1..8 opaque page versions, each at most 128 characters, or exactly ["*"] = the page exists). The version is compared inside the write's transaction under the page row lock: a stale one answers `412 { code: precondition_failed }` with nothing changed; a write that already happened answers `200 { outcome: noop, pageId }` (never for a permanent delete); otherwise `200 { outcome: applied, pageId }` (inside the upstream response envelope). A busy engine (lock or statement timeout, deadlock, too many in flight) answers a retryable `503 { code: engine_busy }`. A fork without these routes answers the framework's plain 404, which an integrator must treat as "upgrade pending", never as page-not-found. Versions and previews (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): the space detail (`getSpace`, `getContentSpace`), every space membership (`listSpaceMembers`, `addSpaceMember`) and a page's ACL (`listPagePermissions`, with `restricted`) carry an opaque `version` (64 hex). `updateSpace`, `archiveSpace`, `changeSpaceMemberRole` and `removeSpaceMember` take an optional `expectedVersion` (a version, or `*` = it exists), compared inside the write's transaction under its row lock: stale → `412 { code: precondition_failed }` with nothing changed; a rename, archive and role change answer the new version. The same holds for the page-ACL routes an integrator relays as the acting user (NOT part of this /api/service surface, inside the upstream `{ data, success }` envelope): `POST /api/pages/restrict`, `remove-restriction`, `add-permission`, `remove-permission`, `update-permission` each take the native body plus an optional `expectedVersion` (the ACL version), run as ONE transaction under a per-page lock, and answer `{ restricted | success, version, effect: { restrictedBefore, restrictedAfter, added[], changed[], removed[], retainedRole? } }` (grantees as Docmost user / group ids). `POST /api/pages/restriction-preview` `{ pageId, action: restrict | unrestrict | add | remove | update, …that route's body }` runs the real write and rolls it back (nothing survives — no row, no outbox row, no cache invalidation) and answers `{ outcome: would_apply | noop | refused, code?, version (the CURRENT one), effect }`; `previewSpaceMember` is its member-write twin here. A preview is never a narrowing route. A busy engine answers a retryable `503 { code: engine_busy }`. Keyed creates (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): `createSpace` takes an optional `idempotencyKey` + `idempotencyNamespace` + `fingerprint` (all three or none) and records the key in the space insert's own transaction, bound to the workspace, the authenticating service credential and the creator; a repeat answers the space it created with `replayed: true` and re-runs nothing, the same key with another fingerprint is `409 { code: idempotency_key_reused }`. Its page twin, relayed as the acting user (NOT part of this /api/service surface, inside the upstream envelope), is `POST /api/pages/idempotent-create`. Import helpers (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616; scope `pages:import:read`, its own smaller rate bucket): `validateImportContent` parses each item exactly as a create would and answers per-item `ok` or a code, never content; `pageTitleCandidates` answers the live children of a parent whose title is an input title or `<title> (n)`, as ids and indices only.

servers.description: The Docmost fork base URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000 in dev). The global prefix /api is included in the paths below.

tags.name: service-bridge
tags.description: Shadow-user provisioning and session brokerage (authentication, not authorization).

tags.name: workspace
tags.description: Canonical-workspace resolution and platform-governed workspace settings.

tags.name: spaces
tags.description: The platform-governed space + membership control plane (data only; the platform authorizes first).

tags.name: pages
tags.description: Bounded page lookups (structural) for the platform's authorization + content reads.

tags.name: content
tags.description: The /v1 filter-then-retrieve read model (privileged data plane; trusts the platform's authorized id set).

tags.name: attachments
tags.description: Read-only attachment lookups (resolve attachment→page + list a page's file attachments) for the platform's /v1 attachment surface; the bytes ride Docmost's native file endpoint.

tags.name: changes
tags.description: The authz change feed + snapshot the platform drains to project membership/page/restriction changes into its PDP (Group D; replaces the platform's direct Docmost-DB outbox).

post.summary: Provision (idempotently) a fork-local shadow user for an external identity.
post.description: Create-or-return a shadow user for the caller's externalId in the fork's own default workspace, with role=member and an unusable password. Idempotent on (derived shadow email, workspace). Scope: users:provision.

200.description: The provisioned (or existing) shadow user and the fork's resolved workspace.

post.summary: Resolve a Docmost user id to its workspace (existence check).
post.description: Read-only lookup of the workspace a Docmost user belongs to. Used by the platform to reverse-provision a PDP anchor for a Docmost-native user it has no mapping for. Scope: users:resolve.

200.description: The user's workspace id.

post.summary: Look up the shadow user ids of platform identities, WITHOUT provisioning.
post.description: Read-only (#486): one entry per requested externalId, in order; userId is null when no shadow user exists (soft-deleted shadow users included — a grant can still reference one). Never creates or revives a user. Used by the platform to reach a page grant whose holder it has no cached mapping for. Scope: users:resolve.

200.description: One entry per requested id.

post.summary: Mint a Docmost session cookie for a fork-owned shadow member.
post.description: Look up the shadow user by the email derived from externalId, verify it is a mintable shadow member (shadow namespace, role=member, not deleted), and mint a Docmost session. Returns { ok: true } and sets the session cookie: over an https edge `__Host-authToken` (httpOnly, sameSite=lax, path=/, Secure, host-only — see wiki-v2 #310), or the un-prefixed `authToken` over http. The platform rejects a non-`__Host-` fork cookie in production posture (fail-closed). Scope: session:mint. There is NO generic impersonation: a non-shadow / non-member / deleted / unknown subject is 403.

200.description: Session minted; the session cookie is set via Set-Cookie.

Set-Cookie.description: Over https: __Host-authToken=<jwt>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Secure (host-only, #310). Over http: authToken=<jwt>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/.

403.description: Not a mintable shadow user (unknown, deleted, wrong role, or outside the shadow namespace).

post.summary: Deactivate a shadow user + revoke its live sessions and collab sockets (#455).
post.description: Fork-side instant revocation for account disable. Look up the shadow user by the email derived from externalId; if present, set deactivatedAt (the isUserDisabled predicate every fork auth entrypoint enforces) and revoke its live user_sessions in one transaction. The platform then force-disconnects the user's live REALTIME sockets (collab editor + notifications/tree) via /api/collab/force-disconnect-user. So a disabled platform identity can no longer read/write wiki content through an already-issued fork credential: /api/* is cut on the next request, new collab/notifications connections are refused, live ones are dropped, and re-mint is refused. Idempotent; a never-provisioned identity is a benign no-op success ({ deactivated: false }). Scope: session:revoke.

200.description: Deactivation applied (or a no-op for a never-provisioned identity).

userId.description: The resolved fork shadow-user id (null for a never-provisioned identity). The caller passes it to /api/collab/force-disconnect-user.

post.summary: Reactivate a shadow user on account re-enable (#455).
post.description: Paired with session/revoke: clear deactivatedAt for the shadow user derived from externalId so a re-enabled identity can sign in and edit again (the mint path otherwise refuses a still-deactivated shadow user forever). Touches only deactivatedAt (never deletedAt) and revives no sessions/keys/tokens (those are terminally revoked platform-side, #117). Idempotent; a no-op ({ reactivated: false }) when there is no shadow user or it is already active. Scope: session:restore.

200.description: Reactivation applied (or a no-op if already active / no shadow user).

get.summary: The fork's canonical (oldest non-deleted) workspace id.
get.description: The single source of truth for the canonical workspace id in this single-tenant deployment. Scope: workspace:read.

200.description: The canonical workspace id.

get.summary: Read the workspace name + default page-edit mode.

200.description: The current settings.

patch.summary: Update the workspace name and/or default page-edit mode.
patch.description: Partial update; the settings JSONB is shallow-merged (sibling keys preserved). The platform authorizes workspace#administer first. Scope: workspace:settings:write.

200.description: The updated settings.

get.description: Archived spaces are hidden unless includeArchived=true. Scope: spaces:read.

200.description: Spaces in the workspace.

post.summary: Create a space and add the creator as its admin member (atomically).
post.description: Both the space row and the creator-admin member row are written in ONE transaction so the outbox projects them together. The creator is resolved from creatorExternalId. Keyed create (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): with `idempotencyKey` + `idempotencyNamespace` + `fingerprint` (all three or none) the key is recorded in the fork's idempotency ledger in the space insert's own transaction, for at least 24h, bound to the workspace, the service credential that authenticated the call, the creator (the acting human, as its shadow user) and `idempotencyNamespace` — so no other caller can ever be answered this space. First use → the created space with `replayed: false`; the same key and fingerprint again → the space that call created (archived or not) with `replayed: true`, and NOTHING re-runs (no space or member row, no outbox row; only the creator's idempotent shadow-user upsert runs, as on every call); the same key with another fingerprint → 409 `idempotency_key_reused`; that space since removed → 404 `idempotency_resource_gone`; a same-key call still in flight past the lock bound → 503 `engine_busy`. A keyed create skips the friendly slug pre-check (its own committed space holds the slug); a slug held by another space is still a 409. Without the key: unchanged, and the body carries no `replayed`. Scope: spaces:write.

200.description: The created space (or, on a keyed replay, the space the key created).

replayed.description: Present only on a keyed create (1.9.0, #616): false = this call created the space; true = an earlier call with the same key did, and nothing was re-run.

get.description: Also carries the space's `version` (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): the value a rename or archive sends back as `expectedVersion`. Scope: spaces:read.

200.description: The space.

patch.summary: Rename / re-describe a space (slug is stable).
patch.description: Answers the space's new `version`. With `expectedVersion` (1.9.0, #616) the space row is locked and the version compared first: stale → 412 `precondition_failed`, nothing changed. Scope: spaces:write.

post.summary: Archive a space (reversible soft-delete).
post.description: Narrows access (a plain member loses the space), so the response carries Authz-Propagation. Answers the archived space's `version`. The body is optional (none = as before); with `expectedVersion` (1.9.0, #616) the version is compared under the space row lock: stale → 412 `precondition_failed`, nothing changed. Scope: spaces:write.

post.summary: Restore an archived space.
post.description: 409 when the space is a personal space whose owner already has an active personal space (one live personal space per owner); the message names no owner. Scope: spaces:write.

get.description: Returns Docmost user/group ids ONLY; the platform maps user ids back to its own identities. Opt-in keyset paging: send `limit` (+ optional `beforeCreatedAt`/`beforeId` cursor) to page over `(created_at, id)` ascending — up to limit+1 rows; omit `limit` for all members (the default). The response shape is unchanged (a bare array) either way. Each member carries its `version` (1.9.0, #616): what a role change or removal sends back as `expectedVersion`. Scope: spaces:read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Opt-in: page size (returns up to limit+1); omit for all rows.

parameters.name: beforeCreatedAt
parameters.description: Keyset cursor bound (last kept row's createdAt). Requires beforeId + limit.

parameters.name: beforeId
parameters.description: Keyset cursor tiebreak (last kept row's id). Requires beforeCreatedAt + limit.

200.description: The space members.

post.summary: Add (or re-add / re-role) a shadow user as a space member.
post.description: The member + adder are resolved from their externalIds. An UPSERT: an existing member (a soft-deleted one included) is re-roled, so this can also demote. It runs under the space row lock and refuses (403, code `self_grant`) adding yourself or raising your own membership (member == adder; a soft-deleted row ranks as none), and (409) demoting the last live admin. Answers the membership's `version` (1.9.0, #616); an add takes no `expectedVersion` (there is no version before it). Scope: spaces:write.

200.description: The upserted member.

post.summary: What a member add / role change / removal would do (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616).
post.description: Decided exactly as the real write decides it (rule M, the last-admin guard, the `expectedVersion` compare), in a transaction under the same locks that is then rolled back: nothing is written, no shadow user is provisioned (identities are only looked up), no outbox row survives. `version` is the membership's CURRENT version (null when there is no row). A state-dependent refusal is `200 { outcome: refused, code }` — `code` one of `self_grant`, `last_admin`, `member_not_found`, `space_archived`, `precondition_failed`; a missing space is a 404 and a malformed body (or a field the action requires, missing) a 400, as on the real route. Not a narrowing route (no Authz-Propagation). A fork without this route answers the framework's plain 404 — never read that as space-not-found. Scope: spaces:write (the scope of the write it previews).

200.description: The preview.

patch.description: The acting identity (actorExternalId) is REQUIRED — a request without it is a 400. Under the space row lock: 404 when memberId is not a live member of THIS space; 403 (code `self_grant`) when the row covers the actor (their own user row, or a group row they belong to) and the new role outranks its current one — narrowing is allowed; 409 when it would demote the last live admin. Answers the membership's new `version`. With `expectedVersion` (1.9.0, #616) it is compared under the row lock, right after the row is found and before rule M and the last-admin guard: stale → 412 `precondition_failed`, nothing changed. Scope: spaces:write.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a space.
delete.description: Allowed on an archived space too. Removing yourself or a group you belong to is allowed. 409 when the member is the last live admin — on an archived space as well, where a direct admin row is the only administer path left. The body is optional (none = as before); with `expectedVersion` (1.9.0, #616; a soft-deleted row's version is its `live: false` one) the version is compared under the row lock: stale → 412 `precondition_failed`, nothing changed. Scope: spaces:write.

post.summary: Resolve a page's owning space id.
post.description: For @AuthzDerived route checks. Fail-closed 404 on any miss. Scope: pages:read.

200.description: The owning space id.

post.summary: Tree facts for a page-lifecycle decision (#485): restriction lineage, descendants, and an optional target parent.
post.description: FACTS only; the platform decides. Workspace-scoped; includes trashed rows. Every walk is cycle-safe and bounded, and reports incompleteness (`ancestorsComplete`, `descendants.complete`, `target.lineageComplete`) instead of guessing; an incomplete descendant walk sets every descendant flag true. `targetParentPageId`: omitted = no target facts, null = the space root, a uuid = that page. Fail-closed 404 when the page is not in the workspace. Scope: pages:read.

200.description: The page's lifecycle facts.

post.summary: The roots of trashed subtrees in a space, newest first (#485).
post.description: A trashed page is a root when its parent is live, missing, in another space, or absent. A root whose lineage carries a restriction, or whose lineage walk cannot finish, is excluded in SQL before the limit. Keyset on (deletedAt truncated to ms, id::text), descending; returns up to limit+1 rows (the extra row signals more). `deletedBy` is a display name, never a user id. Scope: content:read.

200.description: One page of trashed roots.

post.summary: Would each item parse as a page body? (1.9.0, #616 import helper; parses, writes nothing).
post.description: Each item is parsed exactly as a page create parses it (Markdown → HTML → the network-inert HTML parse → ProseMirror JSON → schema check), sequentially, in the order given; nothing is written and no content, parse error or derived text is ever answered — only `{idx, ok}` or `{idx, ok: false, code}`, one per item, in item order. Codes: `too_large` — the item is over 524288 UTF-8 bytes, OR the call's byte budget ran out before it (1048576 parsed bytes in total, checked before each item; from that item on every item is `too_large`, unparsed); `parse_budget_exceeded` — the call's time budget (4 s of parsing, checked before each item) ran out before it, so it was NOT checked (from that item on every item is `parse_budget_exceeded`, unparsed): a statement about the engine's load, never about the content — retry the same request (the byte budget wins when both are spent at the same item); `empty_content` — the content is empty or whitespace only; `invalid_content` — it does not parse to a valid page body. At most 2 calls parse at once per fork process: a call that gets no slot within 2s answers 503 `engine_busy` (retryable). Scope: pages:import:read (its own, smaller rate bucket).

200.description: One result per item, in item order.

post.summary: Live children of a parent whose title is an input title or `<title> (n)` (1.9.0, #616 import helper).
post.description: Reads the LIVE (not trashed) direct children of `parentPageId` in `spaceId` — or the space's root level when `parentPageId` is omitted or null — in the fork's workspace, and answers each child whose title equals `titles[titleIdx]` exactly (`suffix: null`) or is `${titles[titleIdx]} (${n})` for an integer n ≥ 2 written without leading zeros (`suffix: n`). Exact, case-sensitive and untrimmed. A title repeated in `titles` is answered under its first index. Only ids and indices are answered — never a title — and the integrator must keep only the matches its caller may view. Sorted by titleIdx, then suffix (null first), then pageId. At most 5000 children are read: a parent with more answers 503 `list_too_broad`; a read past its statement bound answers 503 `engine_busy`. A parent that is missing, trashed or in another space simply has no live children here. Scope: pages:import:read.

200.description: The matching children, ids and indices only.

get.summary: The explicit ACL grants on a page.
get.description: page_permissions joined to page_access; grantee by Docmost user/group id (the platform maps user ids to identities). Opt-in keyset paging: send `limit` (+ optional `beforeCreatedAt`/`beforeId` cursor) to page over `(pp.created_at, pp.id)` ascending — up to limit+1 items; omit `limit` for all grants (the default). Since 1.9.0 (wiki-v2 #616) the body also carries `restricted` (the page carries its own restriction) and the ACL's `version` — over the WHOLE ACL, not only the page of items — read with the items from one snapshot; that version is what the page restrict / grant / revoke / re-role routes take as `expectedVersion`. Scope: content:read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Opt-in: page size (returns up to limit+1); omit for all rows.

parameters.name: beforeCreatedAt
parameters.description: Keyset cursor bound (last kept row's createdAt). Requires beforeId + limit.

parameters.name: beforeId
parameters.description: Keyset cursor tiebreak (last kept row's id). Requires beforeCreatedAt + limit.

200.description: The ACL grants, whether the page is restricted, and the ACL version.

post.summary: Filter-then-retrieve page metadata for an authorized id set.
post.description: PRIVILEGED DATA PLANE: returns metadata for EXACTLY the supplied ids (the platform's PDP-authorized set) and does NOT re-authorize. Keyset-ordered by (updated_at desc, id desc); the fork returns up to limit+1 rows so the platform can detect hasMore. Scope: content:read.

200.description: Page summaries (up to limit+1).

post.summary: Filter-then-retrieve space metadata for an authorized id set.
post.description: PRIVILEGED DATA PLANE (see listContentPages). Scope: content:read.

200.description: Space summaries (up to limit+1).

get.summary: A single space's public summary (active only).
get.description: Also carries the space's `version` (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616) — a digest over every field of the summary plus the archived state, so it is a strong validator for this representation and the value a rename or archive takes as `expectedVersion`. Scope: content:read.

200.description: The space summary with its version.

post.summary: Permission-aware full-text search over the pages the caller can see.
post.description: The AUTHORIZATION GATE for /v1 search (unlike the list ops, which are a privileged data plane over an already-authorized id set). PdpSearchService walks the rank-ordered FTS candidate stream in bounded windows and admits ONLY the caller's authorized pages BEFORE the limit/offset slice (filter-then-retrieve; ADR-0005), so a principal too broad to LIST can still SEARCH. The platform passes the caller's Docmost user id and MUST NOT post-filter the result (that reintroduces reverse-index truncation). The hit shape is PII-free: NO creatorId (ADR-0001) and NO rank / total count (no ranking side-channel). Scope: content:search.

200.description: Authorized search hits (rank-ordered, up to limit).

get.summary: Resolve an attachment to its owning page + space.
get.description: Option A (resolve→page): the platform maps attachment→page here, then authorizes page#view/#edit ITSELF (the schema inherits attachment access from the page — no attachment tuple in the PDP). pageId/spaceId are null for non-page attachments (avatars, workspace/space icons, chat uploads), so the platform denies them (no page to authorize). Workspace-scoped, active only; unknown / cross-workspace / soft-deleted → 404. Scope: attachments:read.

200.description: The attachment's owning page + space (null for non-page attachments).

get.summary: List a page's file attachments (compact projection).
get.description: PRIVILEGED DATA PLANE: the platform authorizes page#view BEFORE calling. Returns type='file' rows only (avatars/icons/chat uploads carry no pageId), workspace-scoped and soft-delete-excluded, oldest first. An unknown page returns an empty list (not 404). Opt-in keyset paging (same contract as members/ACL): send `limit` (+ optional `beforeCreatedAt`/`beforeId` cursor) to page over `(created_at, id)` ascending — up to limit+1 rows; omit `limit` for all file attachments (the default). The response shape ({items}) is unchanged either way. Scope: attachments:read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Opt-in: page size (returns up to limit+1); omit for all rows.

parameters.name: beforeCreatedAt
parameters.description: Keyset cursor bound (last kept row's createdAt). Requires beforeId + limit.

parameters.name: beforeId
parameters.description: Keyset cursor tiebreak (last kept row's id). Requires beforeCreatedAt + limit.

200.description: The page's file attachments (possibly empty).

get.summary: Long-poll the authz change feed (membership / page / restriction changes).
get.description: Returns typed change events after the opaque `after` cursor, ordered and gated by (xact_id, id): a row is served ONLY once its inserting transaction is fully settled (xact_id < pg_snapshot_xmin), so delivery is commit-safe and GAP-FREE — never the classic transactional-outbox skip of a lower id that commits after the consumer passed a higher one. The cursor is "<xact_id>.<id>": pass it back verbatim, but when you need to ORDER two cursors (e.g. to answer the optional /sync/settle of authorization-service.openapi.json), compare them as a pair of unsigned 64-bit integers — xact_id first, then id — never as strings ("9.9" is before "10.1"). The event `seq` is diagnostic only, never a cursor. Blocks up to `wait` ms for new events (an internal LISTEN/NOTIFY wakeup) then returns immediately; the durable outbox table is the SOURCE OF TRUTH, so a missed wake or dropped LISTEN is only latency, never lost events. `nextCursor` advances past skipped rows too. A cursor at/below the retention high-water mark returns 409 { stale, head } so the platform REBASELINES (reconcile + reset cursor to the snapshot baseline) rather than silently skipping a GC'd gap. Read-only privileged data plane: the platform owns projection into SpiceDB and the Docmost-user -> principal identity mapping (which never leaves the platform). Scope: changes:read.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque cursor (the last `nextCursor` the platform durably advanced); omit for the first read (from the beginning).

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Max milliseconds to long-poll for new events before returning empty.

200.description: A batch of change events (possibly empty on a long-poll timeout).

409.description: Stale cursor: events after `after` were already GC'd by retention; the platform must rebaseline.

get.summary: Stream the full desired authorization set (for the reconciler's drift repair).
get.description: The current membership / page / restriction state emitted as the SAME typed events the live feed uses (seq=0, removed/deleted=false). Keyset-paginated on each row's IMMUTABLE primary id so a concurrent change during pagination can never cause a false orphan-delete on the platform (fail-open); combined with the platform pinning its PDP snapshot BEFORE reading, drift repair stays fail-closed. The FIRST-page response (no `cursor`) carries `baseline`, the change-feed cursor captured at snapshot start; the platform persists THAT as its change cursor after the reconcile succeeds (never the feed head) so a transaction in-flight at snapshot start is replayed by the live drain, not skipped. Pass `cursor` from the previous response; a null nextCursor means the whole set has been streamed. Scope: changes:read.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

200.description: A page of the desired set.

post.summary: The CURRENT authorization structure of pages (1.7.0, wiki-v2 #545): placement, restriction and restriction lineage.
post.description: Facts only; the platform decides and writes. Exactly one mode: `pageIds` (every id answered, a missing one with `exists: false`), `subtreeRootId` + `limit` (+ `after`: the root's descendants, NOT the root, keyset on id) or `limit` (+ `after`: every page, trashed included, keyset on id). A mix, or neither `pageIds` nor `limit`, is a 400. Each response is ONE SQL statement, so every row describes one committed tree (a row's `parentPageId` and `lineageRestricted` never come from two different states). Walks follow `parent_page_id` through trashed and cross-space rows, stay inside the start page's workspace, are cycle-safe and bounded at 1024 steps (the cycle guard's bound), and never report an unfinished walk as unrestricted. Not workspace-scoped (like the snapshot). Scope: pages:authz:read (its own, larger rate window).

200.description: The pages' state, ordered by id.

post.summary: Re-check every live realtime connection on this node after a narrowing access change (#501).
post.description: Called by the platform right after it projects a narrowing access change (restrict, grant or membership removal/demotion, space archive, group-grant removal, a reconciler repair, an admin demote). The fork re-checks EVERY live connection on this node against the PDP and only NARROWS: a collab connection that lost access, or lost edit on a writable connection, is closed (the client re-authenticates with a fresh decision); a notifications/tree socket leaves every space room it can no longer view, and is disconnected if its user is missing or disabled. It never widens (never makes a connection writable, never joins a room). A PDP failure changes nothing (a bounded number of consecutive failures then narrows). The body is empty: the call cannot be aimed at a user or page. A trailing pass runs 2 s later, and every node also sweeps on its own interval (LIVE_ACCESS_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, default 60000). Node-local: it reaches the node that serves the request; the sweep covers the rest. Replaced /api/collab/force-disconnect (1.5.0). Gated by the x-authz-service-secret header (no per-route scope) plus RemoteOnlyGuard.

200.description: The summary of a pass that started after the request, or { pending: true } when that pass outlived the 5 s bound (the sweep still covers it).

checked.description: Collab connections plus joined space rooms examined.

disconnected.description: Notifications sockets disconnected (user missing or disabled).

unknown.description: Decisions the PDP or DB could not answer this pass (no action taken).

unknownClosed.description: Narrowed because the consecutive-unknown cap was reached.

500.description: The pass failed (logged as LIVE_ACCESS_REVALIDATE_FAILED); the next signal or sweep retries.

post.summary: Force-disconnect ALL of a user's live collab sockets (account disable, #455).
post.description: Close every live REALTIME connection for a user across BOTH planes: the collab editor sockets (Hocuspocus, all documents; node-local) AND the notifications/tree sockets (socket.io; cluster-wide through the Redis adapter). UNLIKE /api/collab/revalidate, this does NOT re-check access: it is invoked only after the platform has deactivated the shadow user via /api/service/session/revoke, a precise whole-identity signal. It closes an already-open connection that the connect-time gate alone cannot cut. Gated by the x-authz-service-secret header (no per-route scope) plus RemoteOnlyGuard.

200.description: The user's live collab sockets were force-closed.

serviceSecret.name: x-authz-service-secret
serviceSecret.description: Shared secret (PLATFORM_AUTHZ_SERVICE_SECRET) sent on every request, compared in constant time.

AuthzPropagation.description: #501: whether the access this request took away is already enforced by the PDP — `confirmed`, or `pending` (committed, not yet shown enforced). Absent = unknown (native mode, or the settle turned off); never read absent as confirmed.

OkNarrowing.description: Success (no body of interest), on a route that can take access away (#501).

OkVersioned.description: Success, with the resource's new version (1.9.0, #616).

OkVersionedNarrowing.description: Success, with the resource's new version (1.9.0, #616), on a route that can take access away (#501).

PreconditionFailed.description: The `expectedVersion` sent is not the resource's current version (1.9.0, #616). Compared inside the write's transaction under its lock; nothing was changed. Re-read and decide again.

UnconfiguredOrBusy.description: As Unconfigured; or (1.9.0, #616) the write could not get its lock in time, was chosen as a deadlock victim or ran past its statement bound — then the body carries code `engine_busy`, nothing was changed, and a retry may succeed.

BadRequest.description: Invalid body (bad shape, unknown key, or a value failing validation).

Forbidden.description: The credential lacks the required per-route scope.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist (or is out of the workspace / archived).

Conflict.description: A uniqueness constraint is already taken (the space slug on create; on restore, the owner's one live personal space).

UnconfiguredBusyOrTooBroad.description: As UnconfiguredOrBusy; or (1.9.0, #616) the parent has more live children than the scan bound — then the body carries code `list_too_broad` (a retry will not help until the parent has fewer children).

CreateSpaceConflict.description: The slug is already taken by another space; or (1.9.0, #616) a keyed create's `idempotencyKey` was already used with a different `fingerprint` — then the body is an IdempotencyKeyReusedError and nothing was written.

IdempotentResourceGone.description: As every route's workspace/mode 404; or (1.9.0, #616) a keyed create's replay whose space no longer exists — then the body is an IdempotencyResourceGoneError.

LastAdmin.description: The write would leave the space with no live admin (user AND group admin rows count; soft-deleted rows do not). Promote another member to admin first.

MemberWriteForbidden.description: Either the credential lacks the required per-route scope, OR the write would add the actor or raise a membership that covers the actor (wiki-v2 #486, rule M) — then the body is a SelfGrantError carrying code `self_grant`; another administrator must make the change (a retry cannot succeed).

Unconfigured.description: No service secret configured on the fork, OR the fork is not in AUTHZ_MODE=remote (fail-closed).

ExternalId.description: The caller's opaque stable identity id; the fork derives the shadow email from it.

ClientIp.description: OPTIONAL platform-resolved client IP (wiki-v2 #330). The caller (platform) resolves the real client address from its own trusted-proxy predicate and passes it so the minted session records where the user signed in from, not the loopback relay peer Docmost sees on this east-west hop. Not validated as an address on the wire (a malformed value must not 400 a sign-in); the fork re-validates with a syntactic IP check and stores NULL for anything absent, malformed, loopback, or unspecified.

name.description: Optional display name for the shadow user.

userId.description: The shadow user's Docmost id, or null when none exists.

SessionExternalIdRequest.description: Body for the session lifecycle side-effects (revoke/restore): externalId only. Unlike MintSessionRequest it carries NO clientIp — these ops record no session — and the fork's ValidationPipe (whitelist) strips any extra field, so this matches the real SessionExternalIdDto exactly.

userId.description: Docmost user id (opaque to the caller).

workspaceId.description: The fork's own default workspace id.

userId.description: Docmost user id (null for a group member).

version.description: The membership's version (1.9.0, #616): what a role change or removal sends back as `expectedVersion`.

idempotencyKey.description: 1.9.0 (#616): makes the create keyed. Only its sha256 is stored.

idempotencyNamespace.description: 1.9.0 (#616): the integrator's opaque key namespace (e.g. its idempotency subject). Required with idempotencyKey.

fingerprint.description: 1.9.0 (#616): sha256 hex of the integrator's stable request body; the same key with a different fingerprint is refused (409 idempotency_key_reused). Required with idempotencyKey.

ExpectedVersionRequest.description: The optional body of archiveSpace and removeSpaceMember (1.9.0, #616).

actorExternalId.description: The acting identity (wiki-v2 #486): compared against the member row to refuse a self-raising write; never written.

SpaceMemberPreviewRequest.description: `action` plus the body of the member write it previews (1.9.0, #616): add → externalId, role, addedByExternalId; update → memberId, role, actorExternalId, expectedVersion?; remove → memberId, expectedVersion?. A field the action does not take is ignored; one it requires but lacks is a 400.

code.description: Present exactly when outcome is refused.

version.description: The membership's CURRENT version; null when there is no membership row (or the refusal came before it was read).

roleBefore.description: The live role now; null when not a live member.

roleAfter.description: The live role after; null when removed. Equals roleBefore when refused.

provisionsAccount.description: An add would first create the member's shadow account (none exists yet). Always false when refused.

position.description: The page's own sibling position (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): a move to the current parent at this position is a no-op.

ids.description: The platform's PDP-authorized id set (the belt). maxItems MUST stay >= the platform's content.maxListAuthorizedIds default (10000) or a well-authorized principal gets a 400; the provider/consumer contract tests enforce this.

spaceId.description: Pages only: scope the list to one space.

parentPageId.description: Pages only: children of this parent.

titleContains.description: Pages only: case-insensitive title substring (ilike; %/_ matched literally).

creatorId.description: Pages only: the page's Docmost creator id (the platform translates identity → docmost id BEFORE calling).

field.description: title is pages-only, name is spaces-only; a cross-resource field is a 400. Always tie-broken by id.

sort.description: Allowlisted sort key + direction; absent → the legacy `updatedAt desc` default (id-tiebroken). The keyset SQL is generalized to the chosen field; text sorts coalesce null → ''.

updatedAt.description: Legacy / timestamp-sort bound (bound as ::timestamptz). Optional so a text-sort cursor still validates.

value.description: Generic cursor-v2 bound for the ACTIVE sort field — a timestamp (updatedAt/createdAt) or the coalesced title/name string.

before.description: The decoded keyset cursor position (cursor encode/decode stays on the platform).

restricted.description: The page carries its own restriction (a `page_access` row).

version.description: The page ACL's version (1.9.0, #616), over the whole ACL.

userId.description: Docmost user id (null for a group grant).
The searching user's Docmost id (the platform's resolved shadow id); search runs AS this user.

query.description: Full-text query. Bounded to defeat pg-tsquery ReDoS; the fork re-clamps limit/offset server-side.

spaceId.description: Restrict to one space; omitted → the user's member spaces (the PDP gate is authoritative either way).

creatorId.description: Restrict to one Docmost creator id (the platform translates identity → docmost id before calling).

space.description: The hit's space (id/name/slug). DELIBERATELY carries NO creatorId and NO rank/score (ADR-0001 / ADR-0005 — no Docmost-user-id or ranking side-channel).

fileSize.description: Bytes (int8 in the DB; coerced to a JSON integer — file sizes stay < 2^53).

AuthzChangeEvent.description: One typed authorization change. `seq` is the outbox cursor on the live feed and 0 in a snapshot. Ids are Docmost ids; the platform maps Docmost user ids to its own principals (that mapping never leaves the platform).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `after` on the next call; advances past skipped (null-mapping) rows so they never re-deliver. Unchanged from `after` when nothing safe followed it.

head.description: Current SAFE frontier as an opaque cursor (max committed-and-settled (xact_id,id)); diagnostic only. Do NOT use it to baseline the first-boot cursor — use the snapshot `baseline`.

oldestPendingAgeMs.description: Age in ms of the oldest safe row still pending after `nextCursor`, or null when caught up; feeds the platform's oldest-unconsumed-age alarm.

dropped.description: 1.6.0 (#501): how many rows in this batch came from a known authz table yet mapped to no event (a mapper/payload defect, logged by the fork as AUTHZ_CHANGE_EVENT_DROPPED). `nextCursor` still advances past them, so those changes were NEVER delivered: record the batch (`after`..`nextCursor`) as skipped until a reconcile repairs it, and never report it enforced. A consumer should read it as 0 when talking to a pre-1.6.0 fork, which does not send it.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when the whole desired set has been streamed.

baseline.description: ONLY on the first page (no incoming cursor): the change-feed cursor "<pg_snapshot_xmin>.0" captured at snapshot start; the platform persists this as its change cursor after a successful reconcile so an in-flight-at-baseline transaction is replayed by the live drain, not skipped. Null on later pages.

after.description: The previous response's `nextAfter`; omit for the first page.

exists.description: False when no row has this id (never created, or purged): the integrator removes everything it projected for the page. The other fields are then null / false / true / false.

restricted.description: The page itself carries a restriction.

lineageRestricted.description: The page OR any ancestor (trashed ones included) is restricted, or the walk did not finish (cycle, unreadable or foreign-workspace parent, depth bound). An integrator projects it so a page's lock never depends on its ancestors' edges having been projected.

lineageComplete.description: The walk reached a root. When false, `parentPageId` leads into a cycle or an unreadable row and should not be projected as an edge.

nextAfter.description: Pass as `after` for the next page of a subtree or keyset read; null when done (always null for `pageIds`).

Version.description: An opaque, fork-issued resource version (1.9.0, wiki-v2 #616): a digest of the resource's state. Only equality is meaningful; send it back unchanged as `expectedVersion`.

ExpectedVersion.description: A version the caller last read, or `*` (the resource exists). Compared inside the write's transaction under its lock; a stale one is a 412 `precondition_failed` with nothing changed. Omit it for the unconditional write.

content.description: Up to 524288 UTF-8 bytes; larger is answered per item as `too_large` (the request body limit bounds the call).

parentPageId.description: Omitted or null: the space's root level.

SelfGrantError.description: The rule-M refusal body (wiki-v2 #486). Unlike Error, `code` IS contractual: the integrating platform maps it to its own `self_grant` problem.

Error.description: Standard Nest exception body; only the HTTP status is contractual.
